an4.30:8.2: This pair is also mentioned in the same way regarding different teachings at [mn117:38.1]() and [sn22.62:13.2](). Nothing is known of them apart from these passages. It is likely that the current discourse is the original context, as it has a satisfying overall form. The Buddha visits the wanderer’s monastery, where he engages them on a topic of fundamental principles that they should all share. Finally he points to ancient teachers in their own tradition who shared the same principles. The passages at MN 117 and SN 22.62 lack such a satisfying context, suggesting this passage was inserted from here. | Ukkalā lay on the Bay of Bengal in the region today called Odisha. It was the origin of the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika who offered the first meal to the Buddha ([pli-tv-kd1:4.2.1](), [an1.248:1.1]()).
